# Adding a day {#sec-add-a-day}

A new teaching day is five files and a block of configuration. This chapter is
the procedure.

## 1. Scaffold it

```bash
make day DAY=2 TITLE="Validation you can defend"
```

or, equivalently:

```bash
python3 scripts/new_day.py --day 2 --title "Validation you can defend" \
    --exercises resampling,metrics
```

That writes `day2-00-overview.qmd`, one chapter per exercise named, and
`day2-99-consolidation.qmd` from `_templates/exercise.qmd`, and registers the
`part:` block in `_quarto.yml`. Re-running it leaves existing files alone, so it
is safe to use again when you add a fourth exercise to a day.

Chapter files live at the **project root**, named `day<N>-<nn>-<slug>.qmd`. They
are not in folders, and that is deliberate: the live code cells fetch
`data/los_data.csv` over HTTP relative to the page, and they write it into the
browser's filesystem at the same path. Keeping pages at the root means one path
string works in the browser, in RStudio and in the worksheet. Put the chapters
one directory down and you need `../data/...` in the browser and `data/...`
locally, which students will trip over for the rest of the module.

## 2. Check it before you publish

```bash
make check
```

`scripts/check_cells.py` catches the faults that render cleanly and then fail in
front of a student: a missing `engine: knitr`, a duplicated exercise key, a
hint or solution with no exercise, an exercise with no `______`, a solution that
cannot run standalone, a data file not mounted into the browser, and a package
missing from the runtime list. The publish workflow runs the same check, so a
push with any of these fails before it reaches students.

## 3. Add any new data to the generator

Append to `scripts/make_data.R`; do not write a second script. One generator
with one seed is what makes every student's copy identical and every expected
value quotable. Then add the new file in two places in `_quarto.yml`: under
`project: resources:` so it is published, and under the top-level `resources:`
so the live cells mount it into the browser filesystem.

## 4. Add a check, if the exercise needs one

`checks/checks.R` and `checks/checks.py` are deliberately small. A new check
wraps `hds_check()`:

```r
check_folds <- function(folds, n_expected = 5) {
  hds_check(paste0("there are ", n_expected, " folds"),
            nrow(folds) == n_expected,
            hint = "check the v = argument of vfold_cv()",
            detail = paste(nrow(folds), "folds"))
}
```

Write the Python twin at the same time. A check that exists in one language only
quietly turns the booklet into a single-language course.

## 5. Build

```bash
quarto render                                      # student site  -> _book/
quarto render --profile instructor                 # staff copy    -> _book-instructor/
python3 scripts/make_worksheet.py --day 2 --profile student
quarto render print/day2-student.qmd --to typst    # printable worksheet
```

Only `_book/` is published. The instructor profile writes elsewhere precisely so
that publishing cannot leak solutions.

## Writing live cells

| You want | Cell header |
|---|---|
| a worked example that runs itself on page load | `#\| autorun: true` |
| a task the student fills in | `#\| exercise: unique-key` |
| the answer, shown behind a button | `#\| exercise: unique-key` + `#\| solution: true` |
| a nudge, shown behind a button | `#\| exercise: unique-key` + `#\| hint: true` |

: {tbl-colwidths="[52,48]"}

Three rules, each learnt the hard way.

1. **Exercise keys must be unique within a page**, and the R and Python versions
   of the same task need different keys — `baseline_r` and `baseline_py`.
2. **A solution cell must run on its own.** Clicking *Solution* replaces the
   editor contents and runs them, so a solution that depends on an import made
   in the exercise cell it replaced will fail. Anything an autorun cell created
   earlier on the page is fine.
3. **Mark blanks `______`**, six underscores. The worksheet generator leaves them
   as they are, so they print as a line to write on.

## Keeping the worksheet under twenty pages

`scripts/make_worksheet.py` drops solutions, hints, instructor blocks and
browser-only notes, and flattens the R/Python tabs into labels, which is most of
the saving. Day 1 comes out at 14 pages for students and 16 for staff. If a day
runs long, the thing to cut is narrative, not tasks: move the discussion into a
`::: {.web-only}` block, where it stays on the site and leaves the paper.

## The house structure, and why each piece is there

| Element | Purpose | What breaks without it |
|---|---|---|
| Objectives as can-do statements | the student can self-assess | "I attended" substitutes for "I can" |
| Worked example with nothing hidden | a correct pipeline seen before one is built | students debug syntax instead of learning the idea |
| Numbered tasks with a stated deliverable | unambiguous done-ness | the strong students finish and the rest stall |
| *Hint*, behind a button | unblocks without answering | either hand-holding or silence |
| *Check yourself* | catches silently wrong objects in seconds | a plausible wrong number survives to the report |
| A control in every exercise | belief in the method, not the output | students trust pipelines because they ran |
| Instructor block, profile-gated | answers, ranges, failures, timings | the answers are either lost or published |
| *Can and cannot claim* | scope discipline, and the hook to the next day | exercises feel like unrelated notebooks |

: {tbl-colwidths="[30,38,32]"}

## Two conventions worth keeping

**Solutions go in `solution: true` cells and instructor commentary in
`content-visible when-profile="instructor"`, never in a collapsed callout.** A
collapsed callout still ships the text inside the student HTML, two clicks away
in the page source.

**Quote expected values as ranges.** `make_data.R` is reproducible, but anyone
who changes an `n` or adds a draw shifts the random stream downstream.
"MAE ≈ 3.2–3.4 days" survives that; "MAE = 3.423" does not.
